Hi Marcus — adding concrete details below (keeps to one paragraph then bullets for engineers):

One-paragraph (audit-ready): When GreenBank submits a GDPR-compliant erasure request via our API or portal, Redwood marks the primary object and all associated backup manifests with a tombstone marker and emits a DeletionEvent token (format: DE-<region>-<unix_ts>-<rand>). The DeletionEvent includes per-region targets and scheduled expunge windows; final confirmation is emitted once every replica acknowledges expunge completion. Restoration from a replica during an uncompleted expunge window is prevented by a restore-guard check which inspects DeletionEvent state and returns a non-recoverable error if the object is tagged for pending expunge. Evidence artifacts: DeletionEvent IDs, per-replica ack lines, and expunge-complete audit entries in our audit-log (audit_stream_id: as:<uuid>).

Engineer bullets:
- Tombstone mechanics: primary dataset tombstone -> backup manifest tombstone -> expunge wave scheduled with priority/region ordering.
- Restore guard: restores check DeletionEvent state and KV tombstone version; if tombstone_version >= restore_point_version, restore is blocked.
- Evidence locations: audit-log (s3://redwood-audit/expunge/YYYY/MM/DD/), deletion-events index (elasticsearch://deletion-events/_doc), and per-region replication-manifest objects (bucket+manifest object keys).
- Timings: typical expunge wave completion for cross-region replicas: 2–6 hours for same-cloud regions, up to 12–18 hours for inter-cloud or high-queue conditions. We include a final confirmation event when all replicas report expunge-complete.

Marcus — thanks for the call yesterday. Summary and next steps below (audit-ready paragraph + artifacts you can attach to your runbook):

Audit-ready paragraph (one paragraph): When GreenBank issues an erasure request, Redwood marks objects and their backup manifests with a tombstone and emits a deletion token (DeletionEvent) that captures per-region expunge targets and scheduled windows. Each region streams per-replica ack events into our audit-log; the DeletionEvent transitions to terminal state only once every replica reports expunge-complete. During the active expunge window, our restore-guard prevents recovery from any replica that would re-materialize a tombstoned object. Evidence to cite: DeletionEvent IDs (DE-GB-1623412345-0x9f), per-replica ack lines in audit-log (s3://redwood-audit/expunge/2026/05/31/), and the replication manifest snapshot id.
